facts.claim: The LLaDA paper (2025), on LLaDA 8B, a masked diffusion language model with 8 billion weights, reports that low-confidence remasking (keeping the surest guesses) consistently does better than random remasking.
LLaDA (Nie et al., 2025) is a Transformer that sees the whole text, the words after a blank as well as before, and on every step guesses all the blanks at once.
LLaDA sets the reply’s length before it starts writing: it begins from a reply of that many blanks, and drops whatever comes after the end-of-text token.

LLaDA (2025) writes a 256-token reply at 1 to 8 tokens a pass and finds that what speed buys depends on the task: on two math tests it matched LLaMA3 8B at 1.5 and 1.8 times its tokens a second, on one coding test it fell behind.
MDLM (2024) found simple masked diffusion works better than previously thought, coming close to left-to-right models at predicting text, and can write text of any length block by block.
SEDD (2023) reports a discrete diffusion language model competitive with GPT-2 at comparable size, and similar quality with 32 times fewer passes of the model.

Fast-dLLM (Wu et al., 2025) traces the quality drop of filling many blanks in one step to guesses made together not seeing each other: two blanks meant for “high card” or “full house” can come out “high house”.

Fast-dLLM (2025) stamps, each pass, only the guesses above a confidence bar instead of a fixed number, and with a reuse of earlier passes’ work reports up to 27.6 times more tokens a second than the same model without them, its accuracy within 1–2 points.

Google DeepMind announced Gemini Diffusion on 20 May 2025 as an experimental research model that turns random noise into text, faster than its fastest model so far, as an experimental demo with a waitlist.
Inception, the vendor, claims its diffusion model Mercury 2 writes 1,009 tokens a second on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs. The vendor’s own figure, from its blog.
